question: Gandhi's friend, the architect Hermann Kallenbach, had a Scottish-born business partner who left Johannesburg for Canada in 1912 and later worked in the office of an architect based in Halifax, Nova Scotia. On what date did that Halifax architect die?

sources.title: Brass Plaque reveals a history of a distinguished man and his architectural firm (The Heritage Portal, Munro & Lev, 2020)
sources.quote: Later Kennedy returned to his profession and worked in the office of the well-known Canadian architectural practice of A R Cobb.

sources.title: Andrew Randall Cobb (The Canadian Encyclopedia)
sources.quote: Andrew Randall Cobb, architect (b at Brooklyn, NY 13 June 1876; d at Halifax 2 June 1943).

notes: 1967 is the partner Kennedy's own death year, a tempting wrong entity.

question: The public teaching hospital in Auckland Park, Johannesburg, that was renamed in 1997 after the anti-apartheid activist Helen Joseph first opened in 1967 under a different name. How many beds did it have when it opened?

sources.title: Heritage inventory 7.4.1 Helen Joseph Hospital (City of Johannesburg)
sources.quote: The former JG Strijdom Hospital was renamed after struggle icon Helen Joseph

sources.title: HIA & CMP Knowledge Precinct Vol. 3, Appendix B (tsica heritage consultants for City of Johannesburg)
sources.quote: J.G. Strijdom Hospital opened with 80 beds

notes: 639 is the modern bed count. The opening figure appears only in a timeline appendix.

question: The Lithuanian-born architect who bought the farm near Johannesburg that Gandhi named after Leo Tolstoy also designed, with his business partner, a Dutch Reformed church in Johannesburg whose foundation stone was laid by General Koos de la Rey. On what date was the first service held in that church?

sources.title: Brass Plaque reveals a history of a distinguished man and his architectural firm (The Heritage Portal, Munro & Lev, 2020)
sources.quote: The best known works of this partnership were the Fairview Dutch Reform Church, in Op den Bergen Street and the St Andrews Presbyterian Church on Commissioner Street.

sources.title: Dutch Reformed Church of Fairview blue plaque (Johannesburg Heritage Foundation)
sources.quote: General de la Rey laid the foundation stone on 2 May 1906 and the first service was held on 26 January 1907.

notes: Sources disagree on the foundation-stone date (2, 5 or 7 May 1906), so the question asks about the first service instead.

question: The architectural firm of Gandhi's friend Hermann Kallenbach changed its name the year after he died. What was the firm's new name?

sources.title: Brass Plaque reveals a history of a distinguished man and his architectural firm (The Heritage Portal, Munro & Lev, 2020)
sources.quote: Hermann Kallenbach passed away in March 1945 and in 1946 the name of the firm changed to Kennedy, Furner, Irvine- Smith and Joubert.

question: The first Greek Orthodox church in Johannesburg was designed in the Byzantine style by an architect who was a close friend of Gandhi. How much, in pounds sterling, did its construction cost?

sources.title: Cathedral of Sts. Constantine and Helen (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: The community took six years to raise the £3,300 for the building

question: The Boksburg hospital now called Tambo Memorial Hospital first opened in 1905 under a different name. How many patients did it have beds for when it opened?

sources.title: Tambo Memorial Hospital (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: On 17 August 1905, the Boksburg-Benoni Hospital (BBH) opened its doors with beds for 70 patients.

question: When planning the Second World War military hospital at Baragwanath near Johannesburg, the bed provision was raised above the original plan because of the war in the Middle East. How many beds was provision finally made for?

sources.title: Imperial Military Hospital, Baragwanath (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: it was then decided to make provision for 1,544 beds (instead of 1,200)

question: Johannesburg's first Reform synagogue, Temple Israel in Hillbrow, was designed by the firm Kallenbach, Kennedy and Furner. On what date was it officially opened?

sources.title: Churches of Johannesburg Pt.2 (Johannesburg 1912, Marc Latilla)
sources.quote: The foundation stone of Temple Israel was laid by the then Mayor of Johannesburg, Councilor Maurice Freeman, on 22 September 1935, with the official opening of the shul taking place on 23 August 1936.

question: Coronation Hospital in Johannesburg, opened in 1944, was later renamed after the activist Rahima Moosa. On what date was it renamed?

sources.title: Rahima Moosa Mother and Child Hospital (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: On 29 September 2008, Coronation Hospital was renamed the Rahima Moosa Mother and Child Hospital

question: After leaving Johannesburg, Hermann Kallenbach's Scottish-born partner worked for a Halifax architect who had studied at MIT and the Ecole des Beaux-Arts. In what year did that architect establish his practice in Halifax?

sources.title: Brass Plaque reveals a history of a distinguished man and his architectural firm (The Heritage Portal, Munro & Lev, 2020)
sources.quote: Later Kennedy returned to his profession and worked in the office of the well-known Canadian architectural practice of A R Cobb.

sources.title: Andrew Randall Cobb (The Canadian Encyclopedia)
sources.quote: returning to Halifax in 1909 and establishing his practice there in 1912.

notes: 1909 is the year he returned to Halifax, not the year he opened his practice.

question: South Africa's first dedicated children's hospital opened in Johannesburg in 1923. How many beds did it have by 1933?
In which Scottish town was Hermann Kallenbach's long-time architectural partner Alexander McFarlane Kennedy born?

sources.title: Brass Plaque reveals a history of a distinguished man and his architectural firm (The Heritage Portal, Munro & Lev, 2020)
sources.quote: He was born in Stirling, Scotland in 1879, making him some eight years younger than Kallenbach.
